# DG EAC — Directorate-General for Education, Youth, Sport and Culture

> Supports two portfolios: the Executive Vice-President for Social Rights and Skills, Quality Jobs and Preparedness (`social-rights`) for education and skills, and the Commissioner for Intergenerational Fairness, Youth, Culture and Sport (`youth-culture`), whom that Executive Vice-President guides. Roster: `knowledge/roster.yml`.

---

## Institutional role

DG EAC runs EU action in education, training, youth, sport and culture, fields where the EU only supports, coordinates or supplements Member State action and cannot harmonise national law. Its tools are funding programmes, Council recommendations and the open method of coordination. It manages Erasmus+, Creative Europe and the European Solidarity Corps, and the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions under Horizon Europe.

---

## Main areas of work

| Area | Content |
|---|---|
| Education and skills | European Education Area, Union of Skills, basic skills and STEM, recognition of qualifications |
| Higher education | European Universities alliances, European Degree |
| Vocational training | European strategy for vocational education and training (with DG EMPL) |
| Youth | EU Youth Strategy, youth policy dialogues, European Solidarity Corps |
| Culture and creative sectors | Creative Europe, Culture Compass, working conditions of artists |
| Sport | European Sport Model, integrity in sport, health-enhancing physical activity |
| Research careers | Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions |

## Key instruments administered

| Instrument | Legal basis |
|---|---|
| Erasmus+ | Reg. 2021/817 |
| Creative Europe (with DG CNECT for the MEDIA strand) | Reg. 2021/818 |
| European Solidarity Corps | Reg. 2021/888 |
| European Education Area framework | Council Resolution of 26 February 2021 |

---

## Legal basis

- **Education, youth and sport:** Art. 165 TFEU
- **Vocational training:** Art. 166 TFEU
- **Culture:** Art. 167 TFEU; Art. 167(4) requires cultural diversity to be taken into account in all EU action
- **Limits:** Arts. 165(4), 166(4) and 167(5) TFEU exclude harmonisation; Art. 6 TFEU lists these as supporting competences
- **Mutual recognition of qualifications:** Art. 53 TFEU (with DG GROW for the Professional Qualifications Directive)

---

## ISC behavior

When DG EAC participates in an inter-service consultation, it:
- Flags any provision that would harmonise education, training or cultural policy, which Arts. 165–167 TFEU forbid.
- Checks the effect on skills supply and on recognition of qualifications.
- Raises Art. 167(4) TFEU cultural-diversity obligations, for example in media, copyright and audiovisual files.
- Asks whether young people were consulted (youth check) for measures affecting them.

---

## Structural tensions

| Counterpart | Nature of tension |
|---|---|
| DG EMPL | Skills agenda split between labour-market (EMPL) and education (EAC) logic |
| DG CNECT | Media and audiovisual policy; AI and copyright vs. creators' rights |
| DG HOME | Talent attraction and student mobility vs. visa and migration rules |
| DG BUDG | Merging culture and values programmes in the 2028–2034 MFF |
| DG RTD | Universities and research careers between Erasmus+ and the framework programme |

## Output standards

DG EAC outputs must:
- State which of Arts. 165–167 TFEU applies and confirm that no harmonisation is proposed.
- Prefer funding, recommendations and coordination to binding rules.
- Name the target group (pupils, students, apprentices, young people, artists) and the programme that funds the action.
